My wife and I are moving to a new region soon, and we absolutely require reliable high speed internet access for our jobs. I've been going crazy trying to find a link somewhere on the internet that will actually show me a list of service providers in every town(and address) on our list. I've found no shortage of ISP lists, but absolutely none of them have been accurate(or even worked properly).
Where the hell can I find a database of ALL available ISP's for a region/address?

There isn't one. Back in the days of DSL you could go somewhere like Dslreports.com, put in an address and get back a list of providers.. those days are long gone though. You can use something like http://www.broadbandmap.gov which is more or less a collection of providers that are licensed to operate in a specific area. You simply won't however find a single site that will give you accurate service availability info for all carriers. Why is this? Service availability is proprietary data that is kept secret or purposefully obfuscated/incomplete because having the knowledge of where a particular provider can offer service (and what level of service) can give another provider the ability to perform targeted marketing, as well as develop competitive deployment plans.

Your best bet is to ask someone familiar with the area, like a real estate agent, what companies are dominant. Then look up potential addresses on their respective websites. If you are looking at apartment life, call up the management.

I ran into this very conclusion when I moved about five years ago, or so. Tried to go with the big boy DSL around here, but they wouldn't touch me because I was in "comcast territory." My direct neighbor, twenty feet away, has it. Asked him, he said he bundled it with the local phone service. Couple hours later I was waiting for a DSL tech from the very company that shooed me away earlier. Weird stuff.

Anything to not have to deal with Comcast anymore.

Call the isps. Verizon, att, level3, and even smaller companies like cox, comcast, qworst, i mean qwest would be happy to take your money.

All the companies are in competition (just take a look at cellular maps on commercials) so they are ever changing.

So I just wanted to know what you guys consider to be the most beautiful, aweinspiaring or whatever shots in anime.

Inspired by this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WVRJiY8rcc8
[Discussion] What are some cases of great cinematography in anime? Why does it stand out to you?

This is going to be cinematography in its purest form - not necessarily awe-inspiring scenery - just really notable examples I've seen of the use of camera angles and pans and the like.

Yoko's introduction in Gurren Laggan - from the shots hitting the Gunmen pulling back to the distant view of her in the air, the long sweep as she swings around ending with the foreshortened view of the length of the gun propped against her foot, then the cut to her jumping down and sliding to a stop, and the cut to Kamina's and Simon's reactions. It's just cinematography on a grand scale, and it sets such a great tone for her character.

Another, much more mundane example - Mugi in the relay race on Lucky Star. I've always loved the way that was done. It shifts back and forth between the runners and the reactions of the girls and shots of Mugi looking sort of nervous and builds tension. Then as the previous runner is coming around, it shifts to Mugi getting ready, then back to the girls for a last response, then back to Mugi, side view as she's ready to go. Then when the previous runner hands off to her, she takes off running, but the camera sort of lags behind - there are three or four frames as she starts running, with the last couple just her hair flowing in the wind behind her, and only then does it shift to a frontal view of her running. It's a simple trick, but executed perfectly.

Another one that's always stood out to me, though more an ongoing thing than a single incident - the shots of Lain walking along the street in Serial Experiments Lain. Especially in the beginning, they're shot from a considerable distance, and with the ever-present poles and wires and deep (and disturbing) shadows and looming buildings, and the effect is to make her seem just tiny - this terribly vulnerable little speck of a girl toddling through an enormous and sinister world, and that sets the stage so well for the way the story unfolds.

That's the first ones I thought of at least...
